The key mechanic is that once an image matches a rule's tag criteria, it's locked to that rule and removed from consideration by later rules, regardless of whether it ends up expired or kept — so I need to carefully sort images by rule priority order (10, 20, etc.) and track which images each rule claims.

For rule 20, no untagged images exist so rule 10 selects nothing. Rule 20 targets "nightly-" prefixed images, finding three matches, and since the count policy keeps only the 2 newest by push date, I'm sorting them to identify which one falls outside that threshold and gets expired.

Now moving to rule 30, which targets build-* pattern images, and I see there are 12 matching images (build-1 through build-12) to evaluate against this rule's count policy.

Finishing the full list of pushed timestamps, I now sort all twelve builds by date descending to identify which five are newest and which seven should expire.

That confirms rule 30 expires build-1 through build-7, the seven oldest images. Now I'm checking rule 40, which targets tagged images with the "rc-" prefix, looking at rc-0.1 and rc-0.2 and their timestamps.

With a 14-day expiration window for images since push, and rc-0.3 and rc-0.4 pushed around October 21st, I'm calculating they're only about 7.4 days old as of the current time (~Oct 29), so they haven't crossed the 14-day threshold yet.

Moving on to rule 100 at priority 100, which matches any tag status with a count threshold of more than 6 images — I need to work through how ECR's "any" tagStatus rule applies to images not already caught by earlier priority rules.

Once an image matches a rule, it's claimed and skipped by later rules, so nightly, build, and rc images are claimed by rules 20, 30, and 40 even if not expired. That leaves only images not matching any specific rule - the version tags, latest, and hotfix - to fall through to the catch-all rule at priority 100.

Rule 100 keeps the newest 6 of these 7 images by count, expiring only the oldest one. Sorting by push timestamps, v2.1.0 (2026-10-27 12:08:50) is clearly the earliest, so that's the one getting expired.

So rule 100 expires v2.1.0 as well. Combining everything, the total deletion candidates are nightly-20261015 from rule 20, the seven numbered build images from rule 30, and v2.1.0 from rule 100 — nine images in total. This matches AWS's imageCountMoreThan semantics, which keeps the N newest and expires everything older.

I'm also confirming the build-* wildcard pattern correctly catches build-1 through build-12, and verifying that the rc- images pushed Oct 21 are only about 8 days old as of Oct 29, well under the 14-day expiration threshold, so none of them should expire yet.
